title: Regional headroom snapshots and decision rules (capacity + triggers)
summary: Snapshot of headroom and experiments across regions for Q4 2023 plus recommended decision rules. Includes condensed sheet of observed utilization, experiment outcomes for min/max settings, trigger thresholds, and cost/latency tradeoffs.
body:
Context:
We ran a set of targeted experiments across three representative regions (us-west1, eu-central1, ap-southeast1) to validate conservative min/max allocations and alternative trigger rules for bursts and cooling periods. The goal was to maintain 99th pct latency < 350ms for small text-generation workloads while reducing idle GPU hours. This doc condenses the spreadsheet we used, the outcomes, and an actionable rule set for rollout to Dedicated pools.

Key takeaways (short):
- Setting a small reserve headroom (min nodes) per shard reduced 503s during sudden spikes with minimal cost (~2-4% on baseline).
- Aggressive scale-up thresholds (utilization > 70% on sustained 30s) cut tail latency but caused transient overshoot; adding a 6s debounce reduced oscillation.
- Scale-down should include both idle-time and queue-depth conditions to avoid premature downsizing for intermittent bursts.
- ap-southeast1 showed higher cold-start penalty due to fewer pre-warmed nodes in shared pools; we recommend higher min in that region for production-critical customers.

Condensed sheet (rows = region / instance family / workload profile):
| region | gpu-type | shard-name | min-nodes | max-nodes | scale-up-rule | sustained-window | scale-down-rule | cooldown | observed-99p-lat(ms) | avg-util(%) | notes | cost-est-hr |
| us-west1 | A100-80GB | gen-small | 2 | 20 | util>70% & pending>4 | 30s | idle>120s & pending<2 | 180s | 320 | 46 | stable; debounce 6s recommended | $3.40 |
| eu-central1 | A100-80GB | gen-small | 1 | 16 | util>75% | 30s | idle>150s | 240s | 340 | 42 | lower tail SLA during peak traffic; prefer canary pass | $3.60 |
| ap-southeast1 | H100 | gen-small | 3 | 18 | util>65% | 20s | idle>180s & queue==0 | 300s | 360 | 38 | recommend higher min for production; cold-starts costly | $4.20 |
| us-west1 | A100-80GB | rerank-batch | 1 | 8 | queue>10 | 15s | idle>60s | 120s | 280 | 60 | batching-friendly workload; scale quickly for bursts | $1.10 |

Experiment notes (freeform):
- Experiment A (min reserve vs none): toggled min-nodes between 0/1/2 in us-west1 for gen-small over 48h of synthetic sine-burst load (peak ~3.5qps per node). With min=0 we saw 7x more 503s during a sudden 2x request spike; min=2 removed almost all 503s with +2.1% cost.
- Experiment B (sustained-window sweep): Compared sustained-window = {10s, 20s, 30s, 60s}. Short windows (10s) caused repeated scale-ups for short spikes -> oscillation. 30s balanced tail latency and stability; 60s delayed scaling and raised 99p by ~40ms.
- Experiment C (debounce + jitter): Introduced a 6s debounce on scale-up decisions + random jitter (0-3s) before executing scale actions. This eliminated synchronized chain-scaling across shards and reduced transient overshoot events by ~45%.
- Experiment D (combined queue + util trigger): For rerank-batch, queue>10 OR util>70% performed better than util-only; it reduced average latency for queued jobs by ~18%.

Failure modes observed:
- Cascading floor effect: If several shards hit scale-up simultaneously without debounce, the autoscaler overprovisions then scale-downs in waves causing cost spikes and temporary underutilization.
- Region-specific cold penalties: ap-southeast1 warm-up time for H100-backed pods elevated 99p for first 60s after scale-up by ~120ms.
- Misleading avg-util: Average utilization hides tail bursts; rely on queue length + short sustained-window util metric.

Actionable recommended decision rules (draft):
1) Primary scale-up rule (recommended): (queue_length >= 3) OR (sustained_util >= 70% for 30s). Add a 6s debounce before executing scale-up.
2) Primary scale-down rule: (idle_cpu_percentile >= 95 for 180s) AND (queue_length == 0 for 120s). Require at least 2-min stable window before removing last pre-warmed node.
3) Min nodes policy by region: set min-nodes = max(1, ceil(peak-qps-region / per-node-capacity * 0.08)) but cap at 4 for small shards. Practically: us-west1=2, eu-central1=1, ap-southeast1=3 for gen-small pools.
4) Cooldown & rate limits: rate-limit scaling operations to 1 action per shard per 6s, global shard ramp limit of +3 nodes per minute to avoid runaway.
5) Canary rollout: apply new rules to 10% of traffic (canary shards) for 72h with traffic diversion and monitor 99p, 95p, 503-rate, and cost delta.

Sample monitoring queries (pseudo):
- active_queue_per_shard = sum(request_queue_length) by shard
- sustained_util_30s = avg(util_percent) over 30s sliding window
- prewarm_gap = count(nodes where creation_time < now()-300s)
- change_event = rate(scale_up_events[5m])

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- Run canary rollout in staging for 72h (owners: Diego / Priya).
- Add histogram of cold-start latency per instance family to the infra dashboard.
- Simulate extreme fanout spike (10x) against min-nodes=2 to confirm headroom adequacy; prepare rollback guard.
- Update dedicated-pool-contract templates with region-specific min-node guidance for onboarding (work with solutions-eng).

Appendix: compact experiment logs (timestamps omitted for brevity):
- us-west1-gen-small: min=0 -> 503-rate 0.14%; min=2 -> 503-rate 0.004% (cost +2.1%).
- ap-southeast1-H100: scale-up latency median 420ms; first-30s 99p 580ms.
- eu-central1-A100: 30s window -> stable, 60s window -> 99p +40ms.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a condensed working sheet; values are derived from a mix of synthetic load tests and sampled production traces during Nov/Dec 2023. Expect small deltas when retesting on current fleet.
- If we adopt the recommended rules, schedule a billing-impact review with finance for Q1 2024.

Comments: feel free to add inline rows from the full experiment spreadsheet (link above) or file a JIRA if you need an expanded sim with different instance families.
